title: POC Scoping - Benchmark Planning & Harness Integration
customer_attendees: James Wu - Head of ML Eng
next_steps: Send benchmark harness README and sample scripts
Share security docs and SOC2 summary
Schedule on-prem performance run week of 2026-09-14
Customer to confirm dataset and traffic profile by 2026-09-07
action_items: Maya Patel: prepare initial benchmark harness repo + runbook by 2026-09-07
James Wu: share representative scripts and sample corpus by 2026-09-07
Alex Chen: send pricing and pilot contract template by 2026-09-03
summary: Kickoff for benchmark planning and harness integration for a 4-week POC. Agreed success criteria (latency p95 < 350ms for streaming use-case, throughput targets, quality checks), customer will share scripts and dataset, Redwood to provide harness, runbooks, and security docs. Schedule on-prem perf run and follow-up demo.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-01 14:30 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Maya Patel (Redwood); James Wu, Priya Rao, Liam O'Connor (DataHarbor)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. we've got maya our se with me. quick intro round?
[00:08] James Wu: james here, head of ml engineering at dataharbor. we're evaluating inference platforms for our multi-tenant analytics product.
[00:14] Priya Rao: priya, platform eng, i'll own the infra side for the poc.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: liam, cto, i'll be high level but interested in security and cost.
[00:22] Maya Patel: hi all, maya se, i'll lead the benchmark and harness integration.

[00:40] Alex Chen: cool, rough agenda — scoping success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, streaming vs non-streaming differences, security touchpoints, and next steps. sound ok?
[00:48] James Wu: yes.

[01:12] Maya Patel: to set expectations, we usually run two parallel tracks: functional quality checks (that the model outputs meet your evals) and perf runs (latency/throughput). for perf we provide a harness that can run customer scripts or our synthetic load generator. which do you prefer?
[01:28] James Wu: we'll mostly want to run our real inference scripts — they have some pre and post processing and call out to kv cache today. we do have a synthetic profile for throughput too.
[01:36] Priya Rao: plus we have streaming clients for chat and a batch generate path. streaming is critical for the product.

[02:00] Maya Patel: ok good. streaming adds complexity — more open connections, smaller incremental token latencies versus bulk throughput for non-streaming. for success criteria can you share the target SLOs?
[02:10] James Wu: p95 latency for streaming should be under 350 milliseconds end-to-end, and average token cost needs to be under our current baseline which we'll share. throughput for non-streaming batch jobs is ~250 qps, but that's bursty.
[02:28] Alex Chen: that's helpful — we'll map those to server-side metrics (p95 decode latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization). also want to capture quality: we expect no more than 5% drop in relevance on our eval set for the model variant.

[03:05] Liam O'Connor: on security, we need SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration, and VPC peering or private link for the private deployment. is that supported in the POC?
[03:16] Maya Patel: yes — for Dedicated/Private we can do VPC + KMS; for hosted we provide encryption at rest and transit and we can share SOC2 docs. for on-prem runs we have an air-gapped deploy option but that requires extra ops time.

[03:40] James Wu: ideal POC timeline? we want results before end of september if possible.
[03:46] Alex Chen: we can do a 4-week POC. week 0 is integration and harness setup, week 1 functional evals, week 2 perf runs, week 3 tunings and final report. is that aligned?
[03:58] Priya Rao: that works. can we do an on-prem perf run mid-september? our infra team prefers to test against internal network.
[04:06] Maya Patel: yes, we can schedule on-prem runs. we'll need ssh or ephemeral access, and a small infra checklist. i'll send the runbook.

[04:32] [05:00] Maya Patel: about the harness — we support two integration modes: 1) bring-your-own-scripts (we run them in a container on the harness and replay traffic), and 2) use our driver with a protobuf/gRPC load generator that mimics your traffic. both can do streaming and non-streaming. which one best maps to your stack?
[05:18] James Wu: bring-your-own-scripts — our preprocess is pretty heavy so we want to ensure parity.
[05:24] Maya Patel: great. we'll accept scripts as a docker image or a runnable python entry point. we have example adapters in the repo. one note, sometimes customers' scripts call internal services — if so we'll stub those or provide a small mock server.

[06:00] James Wu: our scripts also use a local kv cache and a global redis. will that affect warmup and latency measurements?
[06:08] Maya Patel: good call — we'll coordinate cache warmup. for fairness we recommend three warmup passes for streaming, then the measurement window. we'll capture cold-start and warmed metrics separately.

[06:38] Priya Rao: tokenization differences can change outputs slightly between local and hosted runtimes. any tips?
[06:44] Maya Patel: we usually lock to a specific tokenizer binary/version in the harness and validate token counts during functional tests. we'll include the tokenizer hash in the artifact so you can reproduce. sometimes filenames or model names get transcribed oddly in the logs — just a heads up.

[07:12] Alex Chen: what about model variants — do you want us to test multiple quantization profiles? e.g., fp16 vs 4-bit quant vs 8-bit?
[07:20] James Wu: yes, test at least two variants: high-quality (fp16) and cost-optimized (4-bit). for streaming we want to see quality regression, too.

[07:46] Maya Patel: noted — we'll capture objective metrics (perplexity or BLEU-like for your evals) and subjective spot checks. we'll also track tokens/sec and GPU utilization.

[08:10] [08:30] Liam O'Connor: about cost — can you provide a cost estimate for the POC including run-hours and sample pricing?
[08:36] Alex Chen: yes i'll send a pilot pricing that includes dedicated GPU hours for your on-prem run and hosted fallback. we'll also propose a reserved slot for the perf window to avoid noisy neighbors.

[09:00] James Wu: on the infrastructure side, our network team requires mTLS and whitelisted CIDRs. we want to avoid public endpoints.
[09:08] Maya Patel: we can do VPC peering or private link and support mTLS; we'll include the security checklist and SAML/SSO for team access.

[09:40] [10:00] Priya Rao: about metrics collection — do you ship traces/metrics to our prometheus, or do we pull from your console?
[10:08] Maya Patel: both options exist. by default Redwood Console will show per-route token costs, latencies, and traces; we can also stream metrics to your Prometheus or push an agent to your environment.

[10:36] James Wu: for load profiles, our traffic has two shapes: chat (streaming, continual small messages, ~300 concurrent sessions) and batch inference (spiky, short bursts up to 250 qps). we want both covered.

[11:00] Maya Patel: perfect — we'll define two scenarios in the harness: streaming scenario with 300 concurrent sessions and bursty batch scenario with configurable qps bursts. we'll need sample session logs and payload sizes.

[11:30] Alex Chen: on the logging side, what retention and pii rules do you need?
[11:36] Liam O'Connor: we cannot persist any raw customer PII in third-party systems; for the POC we'll scrub or use synthetic data.
[11:42] Maya Patel: understood — we'll run with scrubbed/synthetic traces and store only telemetry. we'll document what logs are retained.

[12:10] [12:30] James Wu: what about measuring streaming token latencies? we need per-token p95 and end-to-end response latency for the user UX.
[12:38] Maya Patel: harness will emit per-token latencies, request latencies, and also capture websocket RTT. streaming measurement requires finer-grained instrumentation — we already support that in the agent. there might be slight overhead from the harness agent but we'll quantify it with a control run.

[13:05] Priya Rao: how do we handle model rollbacks or fallbacks during the POC if we see instabilities?
[13:12] Maya Patel: we can pin versions and use automatic fallback policies — the harness can be configured to test both primary and fallback variants and record differences.

[13:38] [14:00] Alex Chen: let's capture success criteria explicitly so we can sign off at the end. suggestions from Redwood side: 1) streaming p95 < 350ms end-to-end, 2) non-streaming sustained 200 qps with < 500ms p95, 3) quality regression < 5% on your evals, 4) security checklist completed. agree?
[14:20] James Wu: agree with caveat on 200 vs 250 qps — we'll target 200 sustained and validate bursts to 250.
[14:28] Liam O'Connor: and we want a runbook and rollback plan attached to final report.
[14:34] Alex Chen: yep we'll include runbook and a playbook for rollback.

[15:00] [15:30] Maya Patel: ok integration steps: 1) you share scripts + sample corpus and any external service mocks, 2) we provide harness repo + docker adapter templates, 3) you build or we help build the adapter container, 4) we run warmup and measurement windows, 5) we share results and tuning suggestions. timeline — aim to get scripts by 2026-09-07 to hit a perf window week of 2026-09-14.
[15:54] James Wu: team will prioritize, we can hit that date.

[16:20] [17:00] Priya Rao: what's the expected infra footprint for the harness on-prem? how many machines/GPU?
[17:08] Maya Patel: depends on the model variant. for a 4-bit quant we can do multi-GPU per node; we'll share a sizing table. for the perf window we recommend a 1-2 GPU small cluster plus a driver node to generate load. we'll include exact CPU/memory/NET requirements.

[17:40] Alex Chen: do you have any regulatory constraints that would affect hosting?
[17:46] Liam O'Connor: we have EU customer data, need data residency and audit logs. also SOC2 is necessary.
[17:54] Maya Patel: we can run in eu regions or private deployment. we'll provide SOC2 docs and an audit log export for the POC.

[18:20] [19:00] Maya Patel: a couple of practical pitfalls we've seen: 1) differences between streaming implementations — some clients ripely commit tokens differently which affects p95; 2) tokenization mismatches; 3) pre/post processing latency dominating. we'll instrument and separate those.
[19:34] James Wu: noted — we'll try to isolate model decoding time vs preprocessing.

[20:00] Priya Rao: can you support function/tool calling and structured output validation in the harness? we call an internal toolchain after generation.
[20:12] Maya Patel: yes — we can validate structured outputs against schemas and run post-processing hooks. include those in your adapter.

[20:40] [21:00] Alex Chen: any blockers from Redwood side to run on-prem?
[21:06] Maya Patel: just network/VPN access and the infra footprint approval. if the cluster is air-gapped we'll need the ops lead to coordinate images and credentials.

[21:30] James Wu: we'll loop in our infra ops and security and expect a short checklist.

[22:00] Maya Patel: OK — recap of deliverables from Redwood: harness repo + docker adapter templates, runbook, security checklist, scheduling for on-prem perf run, and pricing/pilot contract. from DataHarbor: scripts/docker image, sample corpus (scrubbed), CIDR/ssh details for on-prem, and confirmation of traffic profiles.

[22:40] Alex Chen: i'll send an email with dates and milestones after this call. maya will own the harness delivery.

[23:10] [23:30] James Wu: could you also share a quick benchmark results template so we know what metrics you'll report?
[23:38] Maya Patel: yes — we'll include a spreadsheet template with p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, and quality eval columns.

[24:00] Liam O'Connor: one more question — competitors mentioned we've seen include Anthropic and AWS Bedrock, just for context. any feature gaps?
[24:10] Alex Chen: we compete on predictable inference economics and the dedicated/private options and first-class streaming support. we'll surface those in the pilot.

[24:40] [25:00] Priya Rao: timeline check — final report end of perf week, is that week-of-09-21?
[25:06] Maya Patel: yes, if perf run is week of 09-14 we can have final tuned report the following week.

[25:40] Alex Chen: ok let's talk troubleshooting: if streaming p95 is high we may tune batching, kv cache policies, or move to different quantization.
[25:52] Maya Patel: and we'll test prefix caching and also try a smaller context window if reasonable.

[26:20] [27:00] James Wu: will you include trace-level logs so we can pinpoint latency sources?
[27:06] Maya Patel: yes — the harness can export traces and spans. we'll map spans to preprocess, model decode, network, etc.

[27:40] Priya Rao: about costs again — if we need sustained reserved capacity for the perf window what's the lead time?
[27:48] Alex Chen: we can reserve capacity in a few days if we have exact windows; longer-term commitments take more procurement but for a short pilot it's straightforward.

[28:20] [29:00] Maya Patel: final open item — sample payload sizes. can you share average prompt lengths, expected response token counts, and any attachments?
[29:12] James Wu: average prompt 80-120 tokens, responses about 40-150 tokens depending on the flow. no binary attachments.

[29:48] Alex Chen: great. any other questions?
[29:54] Liam O'Connor: none from me.

[30:10] James Wu: just to confirm: we'll provide scripts by Sep 7, target perf run Sep 14, final report Sep 21.
[30:20] Alex Chen: yes, and we'll send the harness repo today.

[30:50] Maya Patel: i'll send the adapter examples and the runbook. also note — streaming measurements need a longer warmup; count on an extra 30 minutes for that during the perf window.

[31:20] [32:00] Alex Chen: recap next steps and action items — james to share scripts/corpus and infra details; maya to send harness and runbook and schedule on-prem window; alex to share pricing and contract.
[32:18] James Wu: ok we'll get that over.

[32:44] [34:00] Priya Rao: small nit — our redis is sharded, we may need a local mock to avoid influencing production.
[34:08] Maya Patel: yep we'll stub redis or provide a local mock. please include connection semantics in the adapter.

[34:40] Alex Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links: harness repo, security pack, and the benchmark template.
[34:50] James Wu: thanks.
[35:10] [36:00] Closing note: action items and owners repeated; schedule follow-up meeting for 2026-09-08 to confirm artifacts. thanks all.

[36:30] END
